hyp1.no_claim_reason: no direction for either gene: the title says lipid dysregulation acts 'through LIPC and CETP', the mechanism says their GWAS variants 'alter' lipid metabolism, and both gene steps have polarity unknown

hyp2.note: title: 'Complement C3 activation drives inflammatory damage in AMD' (no aspect word); the mechanism ends at 'progression of AMD through inflammatory pathways', and the falsification acts in an existing AMD mouse model, so the aspect is progression. The chain's last step (hyp2.3) says only 'leads to AMD', read as risk, so the claim has no route

hyp3.note: the mechanism says TNFRSF10A GWAS variants 'increase apoptosis signaling', 'contributing to the loss of retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptors that characterizes AMD progression', so the aspect is progression; the chain starts at the gene. hyp4.no_claim_reason: the hypothesis claims an association of unknown direction ('strongly associated with AMD but through unknown mechanism'); both steps have polarity unknown, so there is no signed effect to test

findings.detail: every citation on a mechanistic step is a GWAS Catalog variant-AMD row; none mentions lipid metabolism, complement activation or apoptosis, so no mechanistic step in the run has support
6 of 11 steps cite nothing, including every step downstream of a gene (lipid dysregulation, complement, inflammation, apoptosis, cell death to AMD)

confidence 'medium' with no citation stating any of its three steps; its only citations are two C3 variant-AMD association rows, one protective (rs11569415-A, beta decrease) and one with no allele (rs2230199-?)

four of the eight cited rows report the named allele as protective (beta decrease: rs2414577-C, rs17231506-T, rs11569415-A, rs13278062-T) and two give no allele (rs2230199-?, rs3750846-?); the run never says which allele raises risk or how any allele changes its gene

rs2414577, cited as LIPC evidence, lies inside ALDH1A2 by the row's own Ensembl context (distance 0) and 22-44 kb 5' of LIPC (the row lists LIPC as the downstream gene); the LIPC mapping is nearest-gene and the run does not note it
two of the three ARMS2 rows (rs3750846, rs10490924) list HTRA1 as an author-reported gene alongside ARMS2; the run attributes the locus to ARMS2 alone and never mentions HTRA1
hyp1.1 and hyp1.2 are parallel steps (LIPC and CETP both lead to lipid metabolism dysregulation), not a chain; hyp1.1's object is not hyp1.2's subject
hyp4.1 ends at AMD, then hyp4.2 restarts at ARMS2 and ends at complement activation, which hyp4 never connects back to AMD (only hyp2's chain continues from complement activation)
both gene steps have polarity unknown and the mechanism says only that variants 'alter' lipid metabolism, so the hypothesis makes no testable directional claim for LIPC or CETP
the hypothesis is an association with an admittedly unknown mechanism; its one signed-looking step (ARMS2 to complement activation) has polarity unknown and no citation
the falsification expects a LIPC+CETP double knockout to reduce lipid accumulation (so the genes would promote it), a direction the chain never states; its perturbation target names only LIPC
the falsification expects ARMS2 overexpression to 'alter' complement activation with expected 'positive', but gives no direction for the readout
the mechanism asserts 'These genes interact directly and share cholesterol metabolism pathways' with no interaction or pathway record cited

hyp2's mechanism claims C3 drives 'progression of AMD', but its chain's last step says only that retinal inflammation and damage 'leads to AMD' (risk), and no step or citation is about progression, so the claim has no route

hyp3's mechanism claims TNFRSF10A contributes to the retinal cell loss 'that characterizes AMD progression', but its chain's last step says only that retinal cell death 'leads to AMD' (risk), and no step or citation is about progression, so the claim has no route
two of the seven question genes (MCF2L2, CACNA1E) are left unexplained, and ARMS2 is explained only by association
'retinal inflammation and damage' is a compound, vague node; split into retinitis (HP:0032118) and retinal degeneration (HP:0000546)

a hypothesis-level association claim (ARMS2 associated with AMD) has no form, since claims must be signed effects; the run's best-supported hypothesis (three genome-wide-significant rows) therefore yields no arm

the guide's 'leads_to with unknown polarity -> no_sign' rule and its 'dysregulates X -> effect pos on abnormal-X phenotype' rule both apply to 'LIPC leads_to lipid metabolism dysregulation (unknown)'; I followed the run's explicit unknown polarity (no_sign)
no HP term for abnormal lipid metabolism in the corpus (HP:0003119 is circulating lipid concentration only); used MP:0013245 'abnormal lipid metabolism' for a human node

GO:0046666 'retinal cell programmed cell death' is defined as death in the developing retina, so it does not fit degenerative cell death in AMD, and GO:1990009 'retinal cell apoptotic process' covers apoptosis only while the run's label is cell death; used a refinement of GO:0008219 cell death in UBERON:0000966 retina

'retinal damage' has only NCIT:C50731 in the corpus, a prefix the format does not accept; grounded to HP:0000546 retinal degeneration, whose definition (progressive loss of RPE and/or neurosensory retinal cells) matches the mechanism's 'damage to retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptors'

gene-level association evidence from GWAS rows has no field for how the variant was assigned to the gene (nearest gene, author-reported, or with a co-reported gene such as HTRA1), nor for evidence on a narrower disease (advanced AMD for an AMD step)

S10, backed by three genome-wide-significant GWAS rows, reaches belief 3/4 and is labelled 'unsupported', the same word as the evidence-free statements at belief 0; there is no verdict between unsupported and established

the three ARMS2 rows are fused as independent, but two come from studies with the same first author (Fritsche LG, 2013 and 2015) and the third (Gorman 2024) pools IAMDGC among its cohorts, so the samples likely overlap

the MONDO AMD definition ('Age-related loss of vision in the central portion of the retina (macula), secondary to retinal degeneration') bears on 'retinal damage leads to AMD', but textbook evidence is for bridges only and the guide does not say whether 'secondary to' is a feature or a cause; not used

the falsification blocks TNFRSF10A and says 'blocking should reduce cell death', reading apoptosis markers, yet its expected field is 'positive' (an increase); hyp1 and hyp2 set the field to the readout's direction (knockout reduces lipid accumulation: negative; inhibition improves photoreceptor survival: positive)

hyp3 cites one accession (rs13278062), below the question's min_evidence_per_hypothesis of 2; all eight citations in the run are GWAS Catalog rows, five of them from one paper (Gorman 2024, PMID 39623103; both of hyp1's citations are from it), although eleven specialists were available and min_sources_per_hypothesis is 2

the GO:0097190 definition ('The series of molecular signals which triggers the apoptotic death of a cell') states hyp3.2's link (apoptotic signaling raises cell death) for any cell, but textbook evidence is for bridges only, so S8 stays at belief 0 although its link holds by definition

the guide takes a claim's sign from the title or mechanism and its disease from the chain's end, but does not say where its aspect comes from when they disagree: hyp2 and hyp3 chains end 'leads to AMD' (risk by default), their mechanisms say 'progression', and their titles ('damage in AMD', 'retinal cell loss in AMD') could be read as severity; the curator used the chain (3 arms at belief 0), the audit the mechanism (no route), as the Alzheimer gemini r2 audit did

audit.reason: the claim's aspect comes from what the hypothesis asserts, like its sign: hyp2's mechanism ends at 'progression of AMD through inflammatory pathways', the falsification acts in an existing AMD mouse model, and the title has no aspect word. The chain's 'leads to AMD' has no aspect word either and was read as risk by default, so the mismatch is a result (no route), not a reason to change the claim. The guide's 'disease the chain concludes' picks the disease, not the aspect. Same call as the Alzheimer gemini r2 audit (H2) and the AMD gemini multi r1 curation (h3_apoptosis). hyp2 arms 2 -> 0

as for hyp2: the mechanism says TNFRSF10A contributes to the loss of RPE and photoreceptors 'that characterizes AMD progression'; hyp3.3 says only 'leads to AMD' ('contributes to AMD pathology'), read as risk. hyp3 arms 1 -> 0; claims with no route 0 -> 2
